semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The term 'deep' in 'deep feed-forward neural network' refers to the presence of multiple layers in the network, which is a specification of the broader category described by 'feed-forward neural networks'. While 'deep' adds a level of specificity, the models are inherently the same in basic structure and operation, just differing in depth.

'Feedforward network' is just another term for 'feed-forward neural networks'. Both terms refer to the same class of neural networks where connections between the nodes do not form a cycle, making them semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: 'Neural network' is a broader category that includes 'feed-forward neural networks' as one of its various architectures. All types of neural networks, including feed-forward, belong under the umbrella term 'neural network'.

closest_parent_model.justification: As 'neural network' is the only parent model identified above, it is by default the Closest Parent Model. It directly encompasses 'feed-forward neural networks' as a subtype within its overall category of various neural architecture designs.

child_models.justification: 'Deep feed-forward neural network' is a more specific type of 'feed-forward neural network', which implies a hierarchy where the 'deep' version can be considered a 'child' due to the additional specification of depth.

closest_child_model.justification: Since 'deep feed-forward neural network' is the only child model, being a more detailed or specific version of 'feed-forward neural networks', it is the closest by default.

sibling_models.justification: 'Multi-layer perceptrons' are a specific type of feed-forward network that includes multiple layers of perceptrons. They fall under the broad category of 'neural networks,' similar to 'feed-forward neural networks' but are different architectures that do not encapsulate or extend the feed-forward networks.

A 'two-layer neural network' is another specific architecture within the broader neural network family and directly comparable as a sibling model due to its specific layer characteristic, similar in specificity to the 'feed-forward' nature.

'Wide neural networks' describe another type of architecture which focuses on width (number of neurons in each layer) rather than the depth of layers, unlike 'feed-forward neural networks', but sharing the non-recurrent and non-convolutional structural paradigms.

closest_sibling_model.justification: 'Multi-layer perceptrons' are conceptually closest to 'feed-forward neural networks' as they are essentially a specific implementation of feed-forward architectures, particularly when structured with multiple layers, making them the most similar sibling by design.

unrelated_models.justification: Recurrent neural networks involve cyclic connections, which is fundamentally different from feed-forward networks that do not allow cycles.
This is a distinct type of recurrent neural network involving second-order connections, differing significantly from feed-forward architectures.
Convolutional neural networks focus on spatial hierarchies using convolutional layers, unlike the layered approach of standard feed-forward networks.

Deep Q-Networks are reinforcement learning models leveraging deep learning - a distinct paradigm not directly related to traditional feed-forward networks.
Bayesian neural networks incorporate probabilistic approaches, adding a layer of complexity not present in straightforward feed-forward networks.

These are specialized networks leveraging residual connections to facilitate learning in deep architectures, differing from pure feed-forward connections.
